Gut microorganisms rely largely on energy derived from the human diet to perform metabolic functions essential for their survival, and the gut microbiome composition therefore rapidly responds to the food we eat [1]. A decrease in the nutrient flow in the gastrointestinal tract, caused by caloric restriction (see Glossary) or fasting, can thus have far-reaching effects on gut microbes and our physiology.
